note.p: Godwin meets Woodcock (probably not for the first time (but certainly the first since he started his Diary)at the funeral of Godwin's mother, Ann Godwin, who died on 13 August 1809. He also meets him with what seem to be Godwin's three brothers, the following day. All subsequent contact with Woodcock after this date is by letter, but no letters have subsequently been found.

Thomas Woodcock of Briston (3 or 4 miles north of Wood Dalling) advertised in Norfolk Chronicle 18.11.1809 for all creditors and debtors of the late Mrs. Ann Godwin of Wood Dalling. In December 1809 he and Godwin's brother Philip Hull Godwin were the contacts for details of land to be sold at auction by James Woodcock. In 1811 he subscribed 1 guinea to the Norfolk and Norwich Auxiliary Bible Society. Norfolk Chronicle 9.5.1812 death of Mr Thomas Woodcock, shopkeeper of Briston. Burial record at Briston, widower age 52.
